title: UK Army Medical Officer Recruitment 2026: Doctor Guide
metaDescription: UK Army doctor 2026: GMC registration, £75,000 bursary, Sandhurst training and pay. Full guide to joining the Royal Army Medical Corps. Apply today.
headline: Serve as a Doctor in the British Army

sections.title: Who can become an Army doctor?
sections.content:
To serve as a doctor in the British Army you need a full medicine degree and registration with the UK General Medical Council (GMC). There are two main routes in: the Defence Undergraduate Cadetship, also called a medical bursary, for students still at medical school, and direct entry for doctors who have completed their foundation years.

The age range for applicants is 17 years and 9 months to 36 years and 11 months. Specialists can apply up to the age of 55. You must pass the Army Officer Selection Board, a medical, and an interview with the Army Medical Services. The process is competitive, so early preparation matters.

sections.title: Bursary and cadetship route
sections.content:
The medical bursary is worth up to £75,000 for candidates who will graduate with an Army-endorsed medical degree and intend to join the Royal Army Medical Corps (RAMC) for at least four years after foundation training. You must be aged between 18 and 39 and apply by the end of January while still at university.

The cadetship scheme sponsors suitable candidates during their last three years at medical school. In return, you commit to a minimum of six years of service after full GMC registration. Direct entrants who join after their foundation years do not receive the bursary, so applying during medical school is usually the better financial route.

sections.title: Training after medical school
sections.content:
After completing foundation year two, Army doctors attend the 10-week Commissioning Course Short at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, from October to December. This earns the Professionally Qualified Officer (PQO) certification. From January to May, they complete the Postgraduate Medical Officers Course (PGMO).

After that, doctors spend a couple of years as General Duties Medical Officers before choosing a specialty. The Army supports specialist training in general practice or a hospital specialty, leading to a Certificate of Completion of Specialist Training. Fitness standards include a mid-thigh pull of 50kg, a medicine ball throw of 2.7m and a beep test level of 5.8.

sections.title: Pay, postings and career
sections.content:
Basic pay for a direct entrant captain after foundation training is currently around £65,000, with extra allowances for deployment, living overseas or qualifying as a GP. Army doctors work in barracks medical centres, field hospitals and on operations alongside regular GPs, consultants and nurses, both in the UK and overseas.

The career offers a mix of clinical work, leadership and adventure that civilian medicine rarely matches. Reservist routes also exist for experienced GPs and consultants, who may apply up to the age of 50, and in some circumstances beyond. The application timeline from first contact to starting training is around 12 months.

faqs.q: What qualifications do you need to be an Army doctor?
faqs.a: You need a full medicine degree and registration with the UK General Medical Council. Students can apply for a bursary during medical school, while qualified doctors join as direct entrants after their foundation years. You must also pass the Army Officer Selection Board, a medical and an interview.

faqs.q: How much is the Army medical bursary?
faqs.a: The full bursary is worth up to £75,000 for candidates who graduate with an Army-endorsed medical degree and commit to at least four years in the Royal Army Medical Corps after foundation training. Applicants must be aged 18 to 39 and apply by the end of January while still at university.

faqs.q: What training do Army doctors do at Sandhurst?
faqs.a: After foundation year two, Army doctors attend the 10-week Commissioning Course Short at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst. They then complete the Postgraduate Medical Officers Course from January to May. After that, they work as General Duties Medical Officers before choosing a specialty.

faqs.q: How much does an Army doctor earn?
faqs.a: Basic pay for a direct entrant captain after foundation training is around £65,000. Extra allowances apply for deployment, living overseas and qualifying as a GP. Pay rises with rank, seniority and specialist qualifications, and the Army also provides housing support and a pension.
